actions.reason: C0001 has coherent RNA/CNV identity evidence (E2F/MYC/G2M proliferation, PTEN/chr10q loss), positive fused boundary separation from all other sets, and moderate resampling stability. A modest CT scanner association exists but does not explain the RNA/CNV signal, so the candidate remains defensible for downstream validation despite residual uncertainty.

C0002 shows the strongest cross-modal consistency, with WSI, WXS, RNA, and CNV all contributing positive cohesion, coherent PBRM1-mutant/BAP1-wildtype biology, positive boundary separation from all sets, and no significant technical confounder association.

C0003 has coherent BAP1-mutant/PBRM1-wildtype identity evidence with good resampling stability and positive boundary separation. A tissue-source-site association and several weakly integrated members remain caveats, but the strong molecular signal is not fully explained by these factors, so retention for downstream validation is defensible.

C0004 lacks significant RNA/CNV findings and its cross-modal support is essentially WXS-only, but it has a strong WXS cohesion signal, positive boundary separation from all other sets, and no technical confounder association. It remains a defensible discovery-stage candidate for downstream validation despite weak multi-modal identity evidence.

C0005 has a coherent VHL-wildtype/PBRM1-wildtype identity with strong WXS cohesion and positive boundary separation from all other sets. Cross-modal support is largely WXS-driven and no technical confounder is evident, so the candidate is retained for downstream validation with residual uncertainty noted.
